s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of systemic illness with fever, respiratory symptoms, and skin lesions
salient_findings: Multifocal alveolar infiltrates on chest radiography and CT
key_facts: 43-year-old man with no significant medical history
4-day history of fever, shaking chills, hemoptysis, and worsening dyspnea
Several months of intermittent night sweats, arthralgias, and 10-kg weight loss
Painful ecchymotic lesion on left calf with similar lesions on abdomen, back, and arms
Recent respiratory illness in 3-year-old son
Temperature 35.3 °C, blood pressure 117/75 mmHg, pulse 112 beats/min, respiratory rate 29 breaths/min
Oxygen saturation 96% on room air
Bilateral wheezes and multiple painful ecchymoses with hemorrhagic bullae
WBC count 9000/mm3, hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL, normal renal and liver function
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein
Negative tests for cryoglobulin, protein C, protein S, rheumatoid factor, and anti–cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies
Positive antinuclear antibody titer, lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgM, and anti–phosphatidylserine IgM
FilmArray respiratory panel positive for respiratory syncytial virus

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Positive lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgM, and anti–phosphatidylserine IgM

shortlist.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic illness with fever, respiratory symptoms, and skin lesions

shortlist.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Asthma-like symptoms, eosinophilia not present but systemic vasculitis possible

shortlist.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Renal and pulmonary involvement possible, despite lack of specific renal findings

shortlist.label: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
shortlist.why_kept: Palpable purpura, abdominal pain, and arthralgias/arthritis

raw.rationale: The patient's positive antinuclear antibody titer, lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgM, and anti–phosphatidylserine IgM, along with the presence of thrombotic paucicellular vasculopathy, are consistent with antiphospholipid syndrome. The patient's symptoms, including fever, hemoptysis, and ecchymotic lesions, can also be explained by this condition.

rejected.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
rejected.why: The patient's lack of significant neutrophils or leukocytoclasia on skin biopsy and negative tests for antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's lack of significant eosinophilia and negative tests for antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
rejected.why: The patient's lack of significant renal involvement and negative tests for antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of significant gastrointestinal symptoms make this diagnosis less likely.
